findings.title: Pinned development dependencies trigger two upstream security advisories
findings.reproduction: Run pnpm audit --audit-level high --json and pnpm audit --json against the reviewed lockfile. No exploit server was started.
findings.expected: The configured high-severity dependency gate should pass, or an explicit reviewed exception should identify the exact unreachable configuration.
findings.observed: npm reports GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp (critical) for vitest 3.2.4 and GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9 (moderate) for both vitest and @vitest/mocker. These are two advisory root causes, not three independent vulnerabilities. Both audit commands exit 1.
findings.impact: The affected packages are development dependencies. Reviewed scripts use vitest run; no first-party UI/API server or public mocker plugin configuration was found. This is a dependency/release-gate defect, not a demonstrated remote compromise of the offline CLI. Project severity is medium; upstream critical severity is retained separately. The second advisory requires a reachable development-server integration. No runtime production dependency advisory was reported by this registry snapshot.
findings.recommendedFix: Upgrade and pin a supported patched Vitest/mocker pair, regenerate the lockfile with the pinned package manager, then review compatibility and rerun tests and both audits. The registry lists >=4.1.11 for the mocker issue. For the first advisory, the registry says >=3.2.6 while the upstream advisory page says 3.2.5; retain this discrepancy and verify the chosen version against fresh authoritative records. Do not blanket-ignore the advisory or expose the test API.
findings.requiredVerification: A fresh registry audit clears both advisory IDs; the updated locked install, tests and CI pass. Confirm no test UI/API endpoint is introduced.

findings.title: Input overwrite protection misses aliases of parent directories
findings.reproduction: Create real/input.txt containing the public zero-entropy mnemonic and a directory symlink alias -> real. Run encode --mode seedshift --mnemonic-file real/input.txt --dates 23-09-2026 --output alias/input.txt. The retained harness performs this only below a temporary audit directory.
findings.expected: Reject output that resolves to the input before processing or publishing it; the input file must retain its bytes.
findings.observed: Exit 0. real/input.txt is replaced by MNC1:seedshift:english:wool abuse actual ... congress. The overlap check compares path strings after resolve(), which does not resolve directory symlinks.
findings.impact: A user can accidentally overwrite the only original input with a transformed record whose separate dates are required for recovery. Alias collisions can also bypass output/output separation. The ordinary writer safely replaces a final-component symlink; that distinct case passes and does not protect aliased parent directories. No attacker-controlled race or host privilege escalation was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Canonicalize existing parents and compare effective destination identities against all input and output paths. Preserve final-symlink replacement semantics, check at the publication boundary, and document the residual concurrent filesystem-race threat. Reject overlap rather than relying only on lexical preflight.
findings.requiredVerification: The retained source-alias CLI reproduction must fail without changing input bytes; cover output aliases, nested paths and non-existing children, while retaining the passing final-symlink and private-permission tests. Remove the expected-failure marker only after fixing production.

findings.title: Valid uppercase Bech32 evidence rejects the correct recovered mnemonic
findings.reproduction: Use the public abandon ... about mnemonic, native-segwit, mainnet, account/branch/index 0, and BC1QCR8TE4KR609GCAWUTMRZA0J4XV80JY8Z306FYU as address evidence.
findings.expected: A valid uppercase Bech32 spelling and its lowercase equivalent identify the same witness program and match the same recovered mnemonic. Mixed-case encodings remain invalid; Base58 must not be lowercased.
findings.observed: The installed address decoder accepts both spellings and returns identical witness hashes. matchBitcoinEvidence reports true for lowercase and false for uppercase because it compares strings directly.
findings.impact: Date-recovery filtering can discard the correct candidate when a valid uppercase receiving address is supplied. No private-key corruption is involved. The failure is reproduced for BIP84; a BIP86 case is recommended, not claimed reproduced.
findings.recommendedFix: Parse and validate address evidence for its network, compare normalized semantic addresses/scripts, and apply case rules specific to Bech32/Bech32m. Keep Base58 case-sensitive.
findings.requiredVerification: Lowercase and uppercase BIP84/BIP86 addresses match; mixed case, wrong checksum, wrong network and different scripts fail clearly. Exercise recover-date through the CLI, not only the matcher.

findings.title: Extended self-test reports success with an empty public-vector catalogue
findings.reproduction: In a disposable installation copy only, replace vectors/mnemocode-v1.json with {"version":1,"vectors":[]} and run self-test.
findings.expected: The extended integrity command rejects a missing required vector catalogue and validates vector modes/schema before claiming that versioned public-vector checks passed.
findings.observed: Exit 0 and PASS 0 public vectors; 75 representation round trips. The loader checks only version and Array.isArray. The mode dispatcher also treats any mode other than direct/seedshift as legacy; this is source evidence, not a separately executed typo-mode experiment.
findings.impact: Accidental catalogue truncation silently removes known-answer coverage. Fixed startup checks and the round-trip matrix still execute, so this does not disable every self-check and is not proof of a cryptographic failure.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate a strict versioned schema and required coverage: unique names, recognized modes, all intended word lengths, required representation fields and pinned metadata. Reject an empty or incomplete required catalogue. Give known-answer checks distinct status from round trips.
findings.requiredVerification: Empty, missing-required, duplicate and unknown-mode fixtures fail with a nonzero exit and specific error; valid vectors still pass. The startup corruption test remains fail-closed.

findings.title: Public JavaScript discriminants are trusted without runtime validation
findings.reproduction: Import the public library from JavaScript. Pass misspelled to parseInput or formatEncoded as the format, or to serializeRecord as its mode/format.
findings.expected: Public entry points reject unsupported discriminants explicitly and cannot emit a container their own reader rejects.
findings.observed: parseInput and formatEncoded return undefined despite declared return types. serializeRecord emits MNC1 records with unsupported mode/format; parseRecord cannot read them.
findings.impact: A JavaScript/configuration consumer can silently receive no output or save an unrecoverable header. Typed callers and normal CLI flags are guarded; this is not evidence of bypassing valid CLI inputs. Related low-level word-count assumptions were observed but are not separate findings.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate supported runtime formats/modes at public boundaries and add exhaustive default errors. Keep unvalidated internal helpers private or document their preconditions.
findings.requiredVerification: Untyped invalid formats/modes throw deterministic non-secret-bearing errors; every valid public representation and existing container continues to round-trip.

findings.title: Three stale regression assertions make the baseline release gate fail
findings.reproduction: Run npm test on the unchanged captured source with normal local subprocess permissions.
findings.expected: Tests enforce current intended semantics: redact unknown tokens, preserve visual PDF content while clearing metadata, and verify QR behavior without counting unrelated decoration.
findings.observed: Baseline: 180 passed, 3 failed, 183 total. Failures expected echoed invalid mnemonic text, fewer than ten fill operators on a decorative front, and byte-identical PDFs despite intentional metadata rewriting.
findings.impact: The baseline CI gate fails even though these three observations do not establish production defects. Weak assertions could also conceal future errors if merely relaxed.
findings.recommendedFix: Authorized during this audit: updated the redaction expectation, compare front drawing streams with QR on/off, and compare page content/dimensions and cleared metadata instead of serialized bytes. Added independent QR decoding checks and retained real Poppler artifact checks. Production was not changed.
findings.requiredVerification: Installed npm run verify passes. Treat the six expected-failure regression tests as six still-failing desired contracts, not as fixes or release acceptance.

findings.title: Packed README links to documentation omitted from the package
findings.reproduction: Run npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts and compare its file list with relative documentation links in the included README and SSKR guide.
findings.expected: Documentation linked from an installed package is included or links to a stable external version of the relevant document.
findings.observed: docs/SSKR.md is included, but docs/card-designs.md, docs/card-identities.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/REVIEW.md are omitted by the package allowlist. All checked relative links resolve in the source checkout.
findings.impact: Users of a packed/local installed distribution cannot open the design, identity and architecture/review help promised by included documentation. The package is private; this audit does not claim a public npm publication exists.
findings.recommendedFix: Include the required maintained guides in package.files or replace package-facing links with stable versioned URLs. Avoid including bulky audit artifacts in runtime distributions by accident.
findings.requiredVerification: Inspect a real temporary tarball or dry-run file list and check every local link from packaged documentation, including nested links.

observations.title: Formatting is consistent; remaining complexity is concentrated in orchestration and rendering
observations.reproduction: Source inspection and scoped measurements; not a reproduced production exploit.
observations.expected: Maintain clear ownership, honest limits and reviewable release evidence.
observations.observed: All 76 baseline owned TS/test/JS-script files match the checked-in Prettier configuration. Maintained source has 63 TS files; the resolved static runtime import graph has no cycles. Metrics found 134 non-null assertions, 30 nested ternaries and 13 functions of at least 70 lines. The 316-line usage function is mostly help text and must not be treated as equivalent to a 117-line renderer. Five Markdown files fail formatting checks, without broken source-checkout links.
observations.impact: The code is modular and substantially easier to inspect than a single monolith. Formatting does not prove understandable contracts: main dispatch, preview/save orchestration and glass/material layout still require careful tracing. Raw counts are review prompts, not defects or a readability score.
observations.recommendedFix: Next readability pass: named renderer/input types, explicit branches for nested layout decisions, small named validation/publishing stages where they have distinct responsibilities, and comments explaining units, entropy-tail modulus, color wire order and ownership. Keep adjacent simple code together; do not split by line count alone. Pin a development formatter command rather than relying on an external cached CLI. Format Markdown in a separate documentation-only change.
observations.requiredVerification: Formatting and type checks plus existing visual fixtures remain unchanged after pure refactoring; reviewers can trace secret input to transform to export without following visual-layout internals.

observations.title: Resource limits and exceptional cleanup need broader adversarial verification
observations.reproduction: Source inspection and scoped measurements; not a reproduced production exploit.
observations.expected: Maintain clear ownership, honest limits and reviewable release evidence.
observations.observed: SSKR records/counts and QR minimum module size have explicit limits. PNG input is read and synchronously decompressed without an application file-size/pixel budget; text input is also read in full. Reviewed code wipes selected owned entropy/random buffers and private derivation nodes in finally blocks. JavaScript strings and all WASM/transitive-library copies cannot be shown erased by these checks.
observations.impact: Large untrusted local inputs may exhaust memory or block the process. No host-exhaustion probe or exploit was attempted. Failure injection after every allocation, RNG failure and WASM panic-memory inspection remain unexecuted; normal negative tests do not establish those properties.
observations.recommendedFix: Set documented input byte/pixel/count budgets before allocation and isolate expensive parsing where appropriate. Add bounded failure injection for RNG, interrupted writes, renderer timeout and cleanup. State practical cleanup limits instead of promising perfect zeroization.
observations.requiredVerification: Bounded over-limit files fail before large allocation; failures leave no published partial output or secret-bearing logs. Inspect owned-buffer cleanup and native failure paths separately.

observations.title: Pinned WASM hashes were verified; canonical rebuild and platform coverage remain incomplete
observations.reproduction: Source inspection and scoped measurements; not a reproduced production exploit.
observations.expected: Maintain clear ownership, honest limits and reviewable release evidence.
observations.observed: All seven pinned bridge/source/lock/declaration/generated-file hashes match. A fresh TypeScript build reproduces all 126 existing dist file hashes. Rust/cargo/rustfmt/wasm-bindgen are unavailable here; no canonical WASM rebuild was executed. Node 24.19.0/Linux was tested; the declared Node >=20 range and Windows/macOS were not. Available pnpm was 11.19.0, while package/CI pin 10.19.0; no fresh frozen install was performed.
observations.impact: Integrity checks establish consistency with local pinned bytes, not independent cryptographic review, provenance of every upstream crate, or reproducibility across machines. A clean Node build does not close native supply-chain evidence gaps.
observations.recommendedFix: Document and execute the canonical pinned native build in a controlled toolchain; compare bytes and licensing/provenance against full upstream revisions. Re-run frozen installation and acceptance on supported Node/platform versions before release.
observations.requiredVerification: Retain exact toolchain/container inputs, full revisions, commands and output hashes; qualify any unavoidable nondeterminism.

limitations: Full-scope audit with incomplete execution, not a fully executed end-to-end certification. All 32 procedure areas have an explicit outcome.
Only public/synthetic secrets were used. No active wallet material, broadcast, publication, push, release or external message was used.
No full Rust/WASM cryptographic review or canonical native rebuild; pinned hashes are integrity evidence only.
No fresh frozen dependency install; pnpm available 11.19.0 differs from pinned 10.19.0. Linux/Node 24 only; other supported versions/platforms unexecuted.

Dependency registry access was initially denied automatically, then explicitly authorized by the user and completed. No dependency update was performed. Security advisory reachability was source-assessed; no vulnerable server was exposed or exploited.
No physical print/phone-scanner validation, exhaustive visual page inspection, resource-exhaustion testing, or exhaustive fault injection.
The initial sandbox suite had 22 failures, many due to subprocess EPERM/empty output. The unchanged host rerun is the authoritative baseline: 3 failures. Both logs are retained.

Initial full render matrix hit the 300-second harness limit with no completed aggregate evidence. The checkpointed retry completed all 128 cases. This was an audit harness timeout, not a reproduced application crash.
At the audited snapshot, six desired regression contracts were marked it.fails and were not counted as corrected behavior. The dated remediation record supersedes that disposition.

The existing tree was dirty and had no Git remote. HEAD alone does not describe the audited source; use the scoped manifest/source archive. Production was unchanged during authorized test remediation.
Temporary harnesses and screenshot artifacts are evidence, not production inputs. Initial cache/output inventory was narrowed before publication; ignored user output contents are excluded.

coverageAssessment.assessment: Good core arithmetic and SSKR negative coverage, insufficient for unconditional release acceptance. The number of vectors alone is not the criterion. Separate independent expected values, same-implementation regression fixtures and same-implementation round trips.
remainingPriorities: Historical priority, completed by the dated follow-up: fix the functional/file-protection findings and turn six expected-failure tests into ordinary passing regressions.

Validate required public catalogue coverage and pin its upstream provenance; add independent known answers beyond a single direct/legacy 12-word fixture. Current checksum-valid Seedshift has one fixed vector at each of five lengths; only direct-12 includes both fingerprints.
Add local Bitcoin evidence coverage across native SegWit/Taproot/legacy/nested profiles, mainnet/testnet and path/passphrase boundaries, including case and malformed-address rules.
Failure injection for RNG unavailable, partially completed image exports, renderer timeout, full disk and interrupted input; bounded malformed/large image/text tests.
QR payload isolation for every SSKR layout and grouped-member length, long personal fields/glyph failures, colors at extremes, and exact partial last groups across all image/PDF forms.
Canonical WASM rebuild, independent cross-implementation SSKR check, fresh pinned package-manager install and supported Node/platform runs.

releaseAssessment.reason: Historical snapshot assessment: open recovery/file-protection defects, a failing dependency gate and native/platform evidence gaps. Commit b71aff4 verifies the product/dependency fixes locally and in GitHub CI; original platform limits remain.
